game: Week 7 CLE@TEN / kickoff not in pack / TEN +2 (CLE -2) / total 37 / weather not saved; rest, travel, venue shell, line movement not in pack

script.base: Book has Cleveland a 2-point road favorite in a 37 total, implied about CLE 19.5 and TEN 17.5: a one-score grind, not a shootout. Tennessee stays in it on Tony Pollard's back (49 carries, 176 yards over weeks 4-6) while Cleveland splits rushes between Quinshon Judkins (31/97) and Deshaun Watson (19/93). Passing stays concentrated — Carnell Tate (24 targets) for Tennessee, Denzel Boston/K.C. Concepcion/Jerry Jeudy (19/15/14 targets) for Cleveland — because neither QB environment is explosive (Watson EPA +0.03 unblitzed and -0.01 vs blitz; Cam Ward -0.24 unblitzed).
script.flip1: Cleveland leads by 10+ at half, kills the clock with Judkins, and Tennessee abandons the run. Judkins' carry count spikes toward or through 45.5 rush yards; Tate and Wandale Robinson targets rise; Pollard's rushing line dies.
script.flip2: Tennessee grabs the lead, or turnovers turn it into a defensive slog under 37. Both teams run, Ward never escapes the no-blitz look he already fails (-0.24 EPA), receiving yards stall, and Pollard is the one skill player who can test Cleveland's 4.51 YPC run defense.

Estime 9, so Judkins is not a bellcow and Watson's legs are a real tax on his rush line. Tennessee carries are Pollard 49 vs Tyjae Spears 5 and Cam Ward 7. Target order is Boston 19, Concepcion 15, Jeudy 14, Harold Fannin 12, Judkins 11 on CLE, and Tate 24, Robinson 19, Spears 11, Calvin Ridley 7 on TEN. Any late scratch of Watson, Jeudy, or Pollard changes a leg; that 90-minute inactive check is not available here.

matchup.shell: Coverage charting not in the pack (no MOFO/MOFC, no man/zone rate), so shell is inferred only from location splits. Tennessee pass YPA allowed: left 8.08 on 62 att, middle 7.0 on 39, right 7.42 on 86. Cleveland: left 6.62 on 74, middle 7.95 on 41, right 6.09 on 90.
matchup.pressure: Tennessee blitzes 23%, Cleveland 24% — neither is a pressure team. Watson is flat vs the blitz (EPA -0.01 on 81 dropbacks vs +0.03 with no blitz), so Tennessee's light blitz does not force a checkdown game. Ward is the opposite: +0.05 vs blitz (n=43) and -0.24 when not blitzed, and Cleveland's 24% blitz rate leaves him mostly in the bad look. Pressure rate and time-to-throw are not in the pack.
matchup.bleeds: Clearest bleed on the slate is Cleveland's run defense: 4.51 YPC allowed and 24 runs of 10+ in 6 games, plus 19 passes of 20+ on 225 att, with the pass hole in the middle (7.95) not on the perimeter (right 6.09, left 6.62). Tennessee is not a run bleed (4.06 YPC, 18 runs of 10+ in 6 games). Tennessee's pass hole is the left side (8.08 YPA) with 18 explosives on 203 att; middle is ordinary at 7.0.
matchup.overlap: Judkins does not attack a weak spot: 3.13 YPC committee back into a Tennessee run defense that is not leaking. Pollard does — 16.3 carries per game into the 4.51 YPC Cleveland front — but 176 rush yards over L3 (58.7/game) sits under a 70.5 line and full YPC transfer only barely clears it, so that lean is dropped, not carded. Jeudy's demonstrated role (14 targets, 124 yards, 139 air yards) is priced at 21.5 against a Tennessee pass defense that bleeds left and has allowed 18 explosives; his alignment vs that left side is not charted, so the overlap is partial and the price gap is the edge. Tate (24 targets, 221 yards, 360 air yards) is Tennessee's primary target but Cleveland's perimeter is not the bleed and Ward's no-blitz EPA plus a 37 total make the over's counter stronger than the read — no Tate leg.

form: Avoiding season averages; L3 only (weeks 4-6), treated as three-game totals. Judkins 31 carries/97 yards (about 10.3 carries and 32.3 rush yards per game, 3.13 YPC) plus 11 targets/49 rec yards — a 45.5 rush line is 13 yards above this role, and Watson's 19/93 shows the efficient rushes are not his. Jeudy 14 targets/124 yards/139 air yards (about 4.7 targets and 41.3 yards per game, ~10 aDOT) is a steady WR role, not a one-target sample, though the pack has no game log to see if one long play inflated the 124. Context, not legs: Tate 24/221/360 is air-yard heavy and boom/bust; Pollard 49/176 rush and 6 targets for 2 yards is a pure rusher at 58.7 rush yards per game; Fannin 12 targets/40 yards (3.3 yards per target) makes 28.5 a regression number, not an edge; Boston 150 yards on 19 targets (50.0/game) sits on his 50.5 line; Concepcion 106/3 = 35.3 vs a 39.5 line, no gap; Robinson 94/3 = 31.3 vs 34.5, no gap. No similar-defense splits, new play-caller, or QB change are in the pack.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Judkins is a committee back at about 10 carries and 3.13 yards per carry (31/97 over the last three), Watson is taking 19 of the rushes, and Tennessee's run defense is not the soft spot at 4.06 YPC with only 18 runs of 10-plus, so 45.5 needs a blowout clock-kill or a breakaway this role has not produced.
edge_players.must_be_true: Watson plays and keeps the designed-run share, Judkins stays near 10 carries rather than 16-plus, and the game stays inside one score so Cleveland is not grinding the fourth quarter.
edge_players.kills_it: Watson inactive or limited as a runner, or Cleveland leads by 10-plus late and Judkins gets 16-18 carries, or one 15-yard run (Tennessee has allowed about 3 runs of 10-plus per game) erases the 13-yard cushion.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Jeudy has a real three-game route share (14 targets, 124 yards, 139 air yards, about 41 yards a game) and Tennessee has not been a defense that erases WR2s (8.08 YPA on the left, 18 passes of 20-plus), so a 21.5 line only holds if his snaps are about to be cut, which this pack does not show.
edge_players.must_be_true: Jeudy is active on a normal snap count like the L3 sample, and Cleveland's modest 19.5 implied total still includes his 4-5 targets rather than funneling every shot to Boston.
edge_players.kills_it: Inactive, snap limit, or a pure run script where Boston (339 air yards over L3) takes the few vertical shots at Tennessee's left-side hole and Jeudy is a decoy.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig in the pack, so nothing can be sized to a model and no probability is above 70% to distrust. Pack rates agree with Judkins under: 32.3 rush yards per game vs 45.5, Tennessee 4.06 YPC and only 18 runs of 10-plus. Jeudy over is a strong read the 21.5 price disagrees with (market median about 20 yards under his 41.3 L3 rate) and inactives are missing — flag, do not cut. Dropped, not carded: Pollard rush over 70.5 is the real overlap (16.3 carries into 4.51 YPC) but only a lean and L3 form (58.7) disagrees, so step 8 drops the lean; Pollard rush+rec under 81.5 is the average talking against that same bleed; Tate over 52.5 fails the pre-mortem (Ward -0.24 EPA unblitzed, Cleveland perimeter YPA 6.09-6.62, total 37); Fannin under 28.5 is just fading 3.3 yards per target back toward the line.

market_rung_price: Main lines only, no alt rungs in the pack: Quinshon Judkins rush yards under 45.5 at -115; Jerry Jeudy receiving yards over 21.5 at -114.5. No passing yards, TDs, or receptions. Short-priced alts not used.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Judkins went over 45.5 because Cleveland led by 10 in the fourth, Watson's legs were saved, and Judkins ground 16 carries at 3.5 YPC for 56, with one 12-yard run that Tennessee's three-per-game 10-plus tendency allows — a script flip, not the base, since Cleveland is only -2. Jeudy stayed under 21.5 because he was inactive or on the snap count the 21.5 line was already pricing, and Boston took the vertical shots at Tennessee's 8.08 left-side hole while Jeudy saw 2 targets for 11 in a 19-point Cleveland output. That inactive check is not in this pack, which is why Jeudy is flagged for the human rather than sized or cut.
slip_story: One grind story for a 37 total and CLE -2: Cleveland does not pull away, the committee holds, and Judkins stays under 45.5 rush yards, while the modest Cleveland pass volume still finds an active Jeudy for more than 21.5 because his L3 role is a 40-yard receiver and Tennessee is not erasing WR2s. These two win together in the base script and do not need opposite games. Do not add Tate over, Pollard over, or a total over — those need a shootout or a Tennessee run-clock script. No TDs, one market per player, depth receivers left off.
